title: Analysing Austrian Parliamentary Speeches by Predicting Party Affiliations
abstract: arXiv:2610.32515v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This paper examines speech characteristics of the Austrian National Council members (CMs). We introduce analysis methodology based on a fine-tuned BERT-Model which assigns to every speech a probability distribution over Austrian parties. These are then aggregated at the speaker and party level. We perform an extensive evaluation to ensure the quality of the generated distributions prior to further analysis. Instead of considering mis-assignments of predicted parties as a performance issue, we leverage them to derive insights about the CMs and political developments. Our findings show that parties that govern together become more similar in their speech characteristics, while, analogously, parties that are in opposition move further away from governing parties. translated_title: 通过预测党派归属分析奥地利议会演讲
translated_abstract: 本文研究了奥地利国民议会议员的演讲特征。我们提出了一种基于微调BERT模型的分析方法，该模型为每篇演讲分配一个关于奥地利各党派的概率分布，并在发言者和党派层面对这些分布进行聚合。在进行深入分析之前，我们进行了广泛的评估以确保生成分布的质量。我们没有将预测党派的错误归类视为性能问题，而是利用这些错误来推导关于议员和政治发展的见解。我们的研究结果表明，共同执政的党派在演讲特征上变得更加相似，而反对党则进一步疏远执政党。此外，转换党派的议员通常只有在换党之后才会调整其演讲特征。最后，我们公开发布了一个包含党派归属预测的数据集。
tldr: 该论文利用微调BERT模型预测奥地利议会演讲的党派归属，发现联合执政党派的演讲特征趋于相似而反对党逐渐疏远，且议员只有在换党后才会改变演讲风格。
en_tdlr: This paper uses a fine-tuned BERT model to predict party affiliations of Austrian parliamentary speeches, revealing that governing coalition parties grow more similar in speech characteristics while opposition parties diverge, and members of parliament adapt their speech style only after switching parties.
